item.title: Current Events - July 22, 2026
item.description:
July 22, 2026 (2026-07-22) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
        • 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
          • The Jordanian military reports that air defenses have intercepted 8 out of 10 projectiles fired by Iran against the country in Aqaba near the Israeli border, with two missiles landing in remote areas. (ABC News) (CBC) (Ynetnews)
        • Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war
          • The General Staff of the Kuwait Army reports that Kuwait's military and air defenses have been actively intercepting "hostile drones" from Iran. (Arab Times Kuwait) (The Times Kuwait)
      • July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
        • The United States military launches Tomahawk missile strikes on Iran's Larak Island. (AFP via Al Arabiya)
        • The U.S. Central Command launches a new round of strikes against Iran, marking the 12th consecutive day of attacks. (AP) (Middle East Eye)
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • Financial Times reports that the tanker Kavomalaes, belonging to Greek shipowner George Prokopiou, was "highly likely" to have been captured in the Strait of Hormuz by Iran two days earlier. (Forbes)
    • Gaza war
      • The Israel Defense Forces and Shin Bet announces that they have killed three Hamas militants in the northern Gaza Strip, including one in the Hamas military wing that took part in the October 7 attacks on Israel. (The Jerusalem Post) (Cleveland Jewish News)
    • Red Sea crisis
      • Seven oil tankers departing Saudi Arabia's port of Yanbu change course away from the Strait of Bab-el-Mandeb after the Houthis announced a blockade on Saudi Arabian ports. (The Washington Post) (Reuters)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • Kordofan campaign
      • UNICEF reports that six people, including two children, have been killed and 30 people including children have been injured in a drone strike on a market in Al-Rahad, North Kordofan, Sudan. (AA)
    • A Chadian official reports that a drone attack from Sudanese territory has attacked positions in Chad, injuring civilians and destroying vehicles and several shops. The attack is the fifth in recent months, following an incursion by Rapid Support Forces last January. (Sudan Tribune)
  • Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir
    • A 35-year-old head constable is shot and killed in a militant attack in Anantnag, Jammu and Kashmir, India. The Resistance Front claims responsibility. (NDTV)
  • Southern Thailand insurgency
    • Five soldiers are killed and six civilians are injured in a mass shooting by ten unknown gunmen at a security checkpoint in Narathiwat province, Thailand. (Al Jazeera)

Business and economy

  • Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
    • 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
      • Oil prices, including Brent Crude and West Texas Intermediate, rise to over US$95 and $86 per barrel, respectively, and the United States average gasoline price rises to $4.06 per gallon, amidst the ongoing conflict. (CNBC) (NBC News)

Disasters and accidents

  • Seven people are killed after a truck collided with a medical transport van in Pernambuco, Brazil. (Xinhua)
  • A Robinson R44 helicopter crashes in Sincan, Ankara, Turkey, killing the pilot and injuring the co-pilot. (Turkiye Today)
  • In the United States, West Virginia governor Patrick Morrisey declares a state of emergency and announces that 100 National Guard troops have been deployed after flash floods caused by torrential rains were reported across the state, including the northern part. (AP) (The Independent)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak
    • The death toll from the ongoing measles outbreak in Bangladesh exceeds past 800. (The Business Standard) (Dhaka Tribune)
  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • African CDC director Jean Kaseya reports that the death toll from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached past 1,000. (AP)
  • 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
    • The number of reported cyclosporiasis cases in the U.S. state of Michigan exceeds 7,000. (Reuters) (WDIV)
  • The fire department of Tokyo, Japan, reports 453 heat-related hospitalizations, its highest daily total since records began in 2010, as a severe heat wave kills one person and leaves four critically ill. The country's Fire and Disaster Management Agency reports at least 14 heat-related deaths nationwide over the previous week. (AFP via Malay Mail)

International relations

  • Saudi Arabia–United States relations, Nuclear program of Saudi Arabia
    • Saudi Arabia and the United States sign a civil nuclear cooperation agreement allowing Saudi Arabia to use U.S. reactor technology, enrich uranium, and reprocess nuclear waste. The pact excludes the IAEA Additional Protocol and proceeds to U.S. congressional review. (AFP via France 24) (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • Stabbing of Salman Rushdie
    • The federal trial against Hadi Matar, the man who attempted to kill author Salman Rushdie in August 2022 in New York, United States, opens. If he is convicted, Matar faces a sentence of life in prison. He is already serving a 25-year state prison sentence in New York. (AP) (The Guardian)
  • Unknown gunmen open fire at a police station in Canindeyú Department, Paraguay, killing three officers and wounding another. (Abc.com)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Delhi Jantar Mantar protests
    • Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi is released after police detained him outside prime minister Narendra Modi's residence yesterday during protests demanding education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and changes to the examination system. (AFP via France 24)

item.title: Current Events - July 15, 2026
item.description:
July 15, 2026 (2026-07-15) (Wednesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
        • 2026 Iran war ceasefire
          • Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says that ceasefire negotiations aimed at ending the war have not closed despite renewed fighting between Iran and the United States. (The New York Times)
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • 2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign
          • 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran
            • The United States Central Command (CENTCOM) says that American forces have redirected two commercial vessels since the blockade resumed. (AA)
            • CENTCOM says that American forces disabled the Curaçao-flagged oil tanker M/T Belma as it was heading towards an Iranian port in the Persian Gulf amidst the blockade. An 18 second video confirms that a U.S. aircraft disabled the vessel. (Stars and Stripes)
        • India in the 2026 Iran war
          • Operation Urja Suraksha
            • India's Directorate General of Shipping warns companies not to deploy Indian sailors onto vessels transiting through the Strait of Hormuz after two Indian seafarers were killed in separate ship attacks in the waterway. (The Indian Express) (Reuters)
        • Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed "until the United States ends its acts of aggression". (Euractiv)
      • 2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region
        • The Directorate General of Counter Terrorism (CTD) of the Kurdistan Region Security Council reports that international coalition forces have intercepted seven drones in Erbil in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. (Kurdistan24)
        • Three drones are reportedly shot down near the U.S. Consulate in Erbil. (Shafaq)
      • CENTCOM announces the U.S. has launched new strikes against Iran for a fifth consecutive day aimed at coastal defense systems, cruise missile storage, and launch sites in the Greater Tunb Island. (AFP via NDTV) (Politico)
    • Gaza war
      • Gaza peace plan
        • Morocco signs an agreement with the Board of Peace to join the International Stabilization Force for Gaza. (Reuters)
      • Nirim attack, Gaza war hostage crisis
        • Israel's military claims to have killed a militant from the Hamas branch Al-Qassam Brigades that participated in the abduction of soldiers Col. Asaf Hamami, St.-Sgt. Tomer Yaakov Ahimas, and Sgt. Kiril Brodski during the October 7 attacks on the Nirim kibbutz. (The Jerusalem Post) (Haaretz)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • Darfur campaign
      • The Sudanese Armed Forces-allied Joint Forces announce that they have recaptured the Orshi Reservoir area in North Darfur, a month after the Rapid Support Forces seized the area. (AA)
    • A drone strike by the Rapid Support Forces hits a power station in the town of Al Dabbah in Sudan's Northern State. (Sudan Tribune)

Disasters and accidents

  • Seven people are killed and one person is missing after a rubber dinghy explodes near Liaoning Province, China. (Xinhua)
  • One person is killed and 24 others are missing after a passenger boat sank off the coast of Sulawesi, Indonesia. (Xinhua)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • The total amount of cases of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceed 2,000. (Medical Xpress)
  • Sudanese cholera epidemic
    • Sudan's Federal Ministry of Health reports that the total amount of cholera cases in north and west Kordofan has increased to 1,547. (Sudan Tribune)

International relations

  • United Kingdom–European Union relations
    • Effect of Brexit on Gibraltar
      • The United Kingdom and the European Union remove the land-border fence between Gibraltar and Spain under a post-Brexit treaty, allowing free movement while introducing joint British-Spanish checks at Gibraltar's airport and port. (AP)

Law and crime

  • Bhutanese refugees scam
    • A district court in Kathmandu, Nepal, sentences former deputy prime minister Top Bahadur Rayamajhi to four years in prison and former home minister Bal Krishna Khand to two years for roles in forging documents for a fraudulent Bhutanese refugee resettlement scheme. (Reuters)
  • Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda conflict
    • The Democratic Republic of the Congo establishes a council composed of mostly international war crimes lawyers to advise state institutions seeking accountability and reparations for victims of violence in the country's east. (Reuters)
  • Detention of Craig and Lindsay Foreman
    • The family of British national Craig Foreman says an Iranian court has added two years to his 10-year espionage prison sentence for speaking to the media, as he and his wife Lindsay continue a hunger strike. (CBS News)
  • Moroccan prosecutors release journalist Ali Lmrabet after questioning him over online posts allegedly defaming unnamed individuals and institutions, while the criminal investigation continues. (Reuters)
  • U.S. president Donald Trump announces that American citizen Dena Karari has been released from Iran after being detained on espionage charges since 2024. Her lawyer, Jared Genser, also confirmed her release. (The Guardian) (NBC News)

Politics and elections

  • France's National Assembly gives final approval to a bill allowing eligible adults with incurable, life-threatening illnesses to obtain lethal medication under strict conditions. The measure awaits Constitutional Council review before taking effect. (AP)

Science and technology

  • Discoveries of exoplanets
    • Astronomers directly image the exoplanet Beta Pictoris d next to its star, located 63 light-years away, using NASA's James Webb Space Telescope and European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope. It is also reported to be fainter than its sibling Beta Pictoris b. The discovery is published in the The Astrophysical Journal. (Space.com) (ABC News)

Sports

  • 2026 FIFA World Cup
    • In association football, Argentina and Spain are facing off in a World Cup final, with the highest-ranked teams in FIFA Men's World Ranking advancing to finals. For the first time ever top two FIFA-ranked teams are meeting in the final since the rankings were introduced in 1992. (Al Jazeera)
  • 2026 ESPY Awards
    • The ESPY Awards is held at the David H. Koch Theater in New York City, New York, U.S., with the 2025–26 New York Knicks winning five awards, including the Best Team award after winning their first NBA championship since 1973, while point guard Jalen Brunson wins the Best Male Athlete and Best Championship Performance awards. (NBC News) (Reuters)

item.title: Current Events - July 28, 2026
item.description:
July 28, 2026 (2026-07-28) (Tuesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Kumamoto earthquake
    • A powerful earthquake, registering at roughly magnitude 7, strikes central Kumamoto Prefecture in Japan, causing a tsunami alert for the western Kyūshū coast. (Japan Wire by Kyodo News)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Victorian Labor Party leadership election
    • Victorian Premier Jacinta Allan resigns, triggering a leadership spill. Ben Carroll is elected unanimously as the new Premier and Victorian Labor Party leader. (ABC News Australia)

item.title: Current Events - July 21, 2026
item.description:
July 21, 2026 (2026-07-21) (Tuesday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
        • 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
          • The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says that they have launched strikes on Amazon's data center in Bahrain. (CNBC)
        • 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
          • The U.S. military confirms that a third service member, identified as 28-year-old Sgt. Angel S Rampersad of New York, was killed during a recent attack on the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, bringing the total American casualties to 18. (Military Times)
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • Malta’s Sustainable Mobility Ministry confirms that the Greek-owned Malta-flagged oil tanker M/T Kavomaleas was "subject to an attack" in the Strait of Hormuz as it was navigating the southern corridor of the waterway. Additionally, all 23 crew members of the vessel are reported to be rescued. (Malta Today)
        • A tanker is attacked by Iran in the coast of Oman near the Strait of Hormuz in the wake of the U.S. military conducting strikes for a 10th consecutive night yesterday, forcing crew to abandon ship. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations also confirms the attack. (Military.com)
      • July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
        • Israeli finance minister Bezalel Smotrich says that Israel will not join the United States in striking Iran. (Middle East Eye)
        • The United States Central Command confirms that they have launched an 11th round of strikes against Iran, against hangars and military targets such as military logistics infrastructure. (The Jerusalem Post) (Reuters)
    • Gaza war
      • The Israeli military and Shin Bet states that senior Hamas Gaza City Brigade commander Adham Ibrahim Shaaban Nasman, who was involved in directing the October 7, 2023, attacks and taking hostages, has been killed in a Israeli airstrike in the city last weekend, despite the ongoing ceasefire. (The Sunday Guardian) (The Times of Israel)
      • Local medics report that 12 Palestinians, including four children, have been killed in airstrikes across Gaza City, in violation of the ongoing ceasefire. (BBC News)
    • Red Sea crisis
      • Two oil tankers departing Saudi Arabia, Xin Long Yang and Rodos, turn around in the Red Sea and head for the Suez Canal instead of the Strait of Bab-el-Mandeb, after a warning by Houthi-controlled Yemen. (Reuters)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • Darfur campaign
      • Around 21 people are reported to be killed in a drone strike by Rapid Support Forces in the Tina region of Sudan's North Darfur state near the border with Chad. (Sudan Tribune)
  • Nigerian bandit conflict
    • A survivor and local official say an armed gang abducted more than 40 people during raids on 11 villages in Maru, Zamfara State, Nigeria, over the weekend. The local government requests additional security forces. (AFP via NDTV)

Business and economy

  • Tariffs in the second Trump administration
    • 2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico
      • A spokesperson for Canadian infrastructure minister Gregor Robertson announces that Canada has cancelled a joint opening ceremony for the Gordie Howe International Bridge that will connect Detroit, Michigan, and Windsor, Ontario, after U.S. president Donald Trump announced 50% tariffs on Canadian goods. (AP) (CBC)
    • Trump announces that imported generic drugs will remain tariff-free until August 2028, face a 100% tariff for one year, and a 200% tariff thereafter, citing efforts to move pharmaceutical production to the country. (AFP via NDTV)

Disasters and accidents

  • A fire on a bus travelling from Lâm Đồng province to Ho Chi Minh City kills seven passengers and injures five others in southern Vietnam. (Reuters)
  • The death toll from the sinking of passenger ferry MV Barima off the coast of Guyana two days ago rises to 53. Seventy-seven others were rescued, while over 55 remain missing. (NEWS Source Guyana) (Demerara Waves) (Guyana Chronicle)
  • The Australian reports that Australian doctor Tareq Kamleh, who traveled to Syria to join the Islamic State, is found alive in a prison in Baghdad, Iraq. (ABC News Australia) (The West Australian)

Health and environment

  • 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
    • The U.S. state of Michigan reports 6,571 cases of cyclosporiasis, which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis. (Reuters)
  • Venezuela's health ministry reports that the hantavirus killed three people in Anzoátegui, says no evidence indicates human-to-human transmission, and rejects any connection to two unexplained deaths among medical workers in Barinas. (AFP via Jamaica Observer)

International relations

  • Lebanon–United States relations
    • U.S. president Donald Trump authorizes U.S. airlines to resume direct flights to Lebanon, ending a suspension imposed after the 1985 hijacking of TWA Flight 847. (The Independent)

Law and crime

  • 2026 Delhi Jantar Mantar protests
    • Indian police detain Lok Sabha opposition leader Rahul Gandhi during education-reform protests in New Delhi after he called for prime minister Narendra Modi's resignation. Parliament adjourns as demonstrators demand accountability for examination scandals and education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's removal. (AFP via The New Zealand Herald) (The Hindu) (The Times of India)
  • Two American tourists are injured, including one seriously, in a stabbing attack near the Acropolis in Athens, Greece. A 60-year-old Greek man is taken into custody. (AP)

Politics and elections

  • Dismissal of Mykhailo Fedorov
    • Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy dismisses commander-in-chief Oleksandr Syrskyi amid protests over the removal of defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov and appoints Joint Forces commander Mykhailo Drapatyi as Syrskyi's replacement. (CNN)
  • Republican People's Party absolute nullity crisis
    • Özgür Özel, the leader of the Turkish opposition Republican People's Party, who was ousted in May by a judicial ruling, announces that he will establish a new political party. (AP) (Al Jazeera)
  • The French Parliament approves legislation allowing limited use of acetamiprid and flupyradifurone, pesticides banned nationally but permitted in the European Union. Environment minister Monique Barbut says she will resign over the measure. (AFP via News.com.au)

Science and technology

  • The wreckage of Pan Am Flight 526A, a Douglas DC-4 that crashed into the sea off Puerto Rico in 1952, killing 52 people, is located by a veteran aviation search team. (The Dallas Express via Yahoo News)

Sports

  • 2026–27 Premier League
    • In association football, Chelsea sign attacking midfielder Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa for a British record transfer fee of £117 million. (BBC Sport)

item.title: Current Events - July 23, 2026
item.description:
July 23, 2026 (2026-07-23) (Thursday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • 2026 United States naval blockade of Iran
          • The United States Central Command (CENTCOM) says it has redirected 12 commercial vessels and disabled one since the naval blockade on Iran resumed on July 14. (Middle East Eye)
        • The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy says it has stopped three oil tankers from passing through the Strait of Hormuz. (AFP via Arab News)
      • July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
        • The Islamic Republic News Agency reports that the U.S. military struck the Shalamcheh area near the Iran–Iraq border. Two people are reported to be killed and 11 are reported injured. (The Guardian) (Middle East Eye)
        • The U.S. CENTCOM reports on X that they have conducted strikes against Iran for a 13th consecutive night amidst clashes over shipping routes, with explosions reported in Ahvaz, Bandar Abbas, and Qeshm Island. (MENA via The New Arab) (WLS-TV)
      • Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war
        • Kuwait's defense ministry reports that a drone has hit the Abdali area near the Iraqi border. (KUNA via Arab Times Kuwait) (Kurdistan24)
    • Red Sea crisis
      • The Houthis claim to have attacked two Saudi Arabian oil tankers in the Red Sea for their violation of the blockade by Yemen's Houthi-led armed forces. There are no reported casualties. (Al Jazeera)
      • Shipping data shows that two Chinese very-large crude carriers carrying four million ​barrels of Saudi Arabian oil, the Singaporean-flagged VLCC Xin Long Yang and Chinese-flagged VLCC Cosnew Lake, are heading towards Bab-el-Mandeb strait. (Reuters)
      • Germany's defence ministry moves the Frankenthal-class minehunter Fulda and the replenishment oiler Mosel from the coast of Djibouti to the eastern Mediterranean Sea, citing uncertainty over a planned Strait of Hormuz mission and concerns about prolonged deployment affecting the vessels. (AFP via Al Arabiya)
      • Reuters reports that Iran sent Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps officers, along with drone- and missile-related equipment, on a Mahan Air flight to Houthi-controlled Yemen on July 13, in preparation for the blockade on Saudi Arabia. (Reuters)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • 2026 Blue Nile campaign
      • Emergency lawyers report that a drone strike has killed several civilians in the Badia area of Sudan's Blue Nile State. (Sudan Tribune)

Business and economy

  • Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
    • 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
      • Oil prices, including Brent Crude and West Texas Intermediate, increase to over US$101 per barrel and to nearly $93 per barrel, respectively, after the escalation in the Red Sea. The United States gasoline national average increases to $4.09 per gallon. (NBC News)
  • Foie gras controversy
    • Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signs a law banning the production and sale of foie gras, citing animal cruelty. The measure effectively ends Brazilian imports of the product. (Reuters)
  • Tariffs in the second Trump administration
    • The United States imposes tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on imports from 60 trading partners, citing forced-labor concerns. The duties take effect Friday and exempt USMCA-covered goods and products already subject to sector-specific tariffs. (AFP via Philippine Daily Inquirer)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 France wildfires
    • More than 20,000 people are evacuated from their homes as wildfires spread in Gironde, France. More than 700 firefighters have been deployed to battle the fires. (BBC News)

Health and environment

  • 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
    • Taylor Farms temporarily suspend operations at its processing facility in central Mexico after American health officials linked it to a current cyclosporiasis outbreak in the U.S., which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis. (Reuters)

Law and crime

  • 2025 shootings of Minnesota legislators
    • United States federal judge John R. Tunheim sentences Vance Boelter to two life terms plus 40 years without parole for killing Minnesota state representative Melissa Hortman and her husband and wounding state senator John Hoffman and his wife in June 2025. (AFP via The Manila Times)
  • International Criminal Court investigation in Darfur
    • The International Criminal Court at The Hague, Netherlands, officially drops charges against former militia leader Abdallah Banda, who was previously charged for his role in a 2007 attack on African Union peacekeepers during Sudan's Darfur conflict. (Reuters)

Politics and elections

  • Reactions to the 2026 Iran war
    • The United States House of Representatives votes 214–208 to approve war powers legislation attempting to require the president of the United States to halt military action against Iran. The United States Senate votes 47–49 to stop the legislation from advancing. (CNBC) (Reuters)

Science and technology

  • The International Mathematical Union awards the 2026 Fields Medals to Yu Deng, John Pardon, Jacob Tsimerman, and Hong Wang at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States. Wang becomes the third woman to receive the prize after Maryam Mirzakhani in 2014 and Maryna Viazovska in 2022. (AFP via Le Monde)

Sports

  • In association football, Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger submit joint bids to host the 2032 Africa Cup of Nations under the Alliance of Sahel States. (BBC Sport)

item.title: Current Events - July 16, 2026
item.description:
July 16, 2026 (2026-07-16) (Thursday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • 2026 Iran war
    • 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
      • 2026 Iran war ceasefire
        • White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says that Iran is still interested in an agreement with the United States. (Reuters)
    • Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war
      • The Kuwaiti defense ministry reports that the military intercepted and destroyed 32 drones entering the country's airspace. (Arab Times Kuwait)
    • The United States Central Command launches new strikes against Iran for a sixth consecutive night in an effort to degrade Iranian military capabilities. (Middle East Eye)
    • Explosions are reported in Iran's Qeshm Island, Bushehr, Ahvaz, and Bandar Abbas, including a bridge in Bandar Khamir. A truck on the bridge is reported to be targeted, killing the driver. (Turkiye Today)
    • Tasnim News Agency reports that American fighter jets attacked the Iranshahr Airport in the Sistan and Baluchestan province. (Ynetnews) (MTV)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • Sudanese refugee crisis
      • Around 1,000 Sudanese returnees in Egypt are reported by a local committee to have returned to Sudan. (Middle East Monitor)
    • The Sudanese Armed Forces says that they have destroyed around 205 combat vehicles, military supply trucks, and four strategic drones belonging to the Rapid Support Forces in the past two weeks. (AA) (Sudan Tribune)

Disasters and accidents

  • Twenty-one people are killed and several others are injured after a bus lost control and veered off the road in Kapchorwa, Uganda. (Xinhua)
  • Fourteen people are killed and several others are injured after a minibus plunged into a deep ravine in Cajamarca, Peru. (Xinhua)
  • Eleven people are killed and 19 more injured in a fire at a care facility in Algiers, Algeria. (BBC News)
  • Six members of a family are killed after a fire engulfed their house in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Province, Pakistan. (Xinhua)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • The Ugandan health ministry reports that Uganda has discharged its last patient diagnosed with Ebola, triggering a 42-day countdown clock on when it can be declared free of the virus. (Reuters)
  • 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
    • The Washington Post links the iceberg lettuce produced by Taylor Farms and supplied to American fast food chain Taco Bell as a source of the current cyclosporiasis outbreak in the United States, which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis. (Reuters) (The Washington Post)
    • Taco Bell removes lettuce from some of their restaurants following reports that the Food and Drug Administration has opened an investigation into iceberg lettuce supplied to them. (The Hill)
    • The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services reports that the amount of hospitalizations in the state linked to the cyclosporiasis outbreak has surpassed more than 100 people. (ABC News)
  • Zambia's health ministry declares an end to its cholera outbreak, which started in August of last year, after four weeks without a case. (Lusaka Times)

International relations

  • Papua New Guinea–Taiwan relations
    • Taiwan says that its representative office in Port Moresby will continue operating and assisting Taiwanese nationals, rejecting Papua New Guinea's decision to close it and stating that the move was made without prior consultation. Papuan foreign minister Justin Tkatchenko says that his ministry informed Taiwan of the closure "weeks ago". (AFP via The Straits Times)
  • Sudan–United Arab Emirates relations, War crimes during the Sudanese civil war
    • Sudanese justice minister Abdallah Dirif says that the government will launch lawsuits against the United Arab Emirates in international courts for its role in supporting war crimes by the Rapid Support Forces in the ongoing civil war. (Sudan Tribune)

Law and crime

  • Corruption in Thailand
    • The Thai interior ministry identifies irregularities in the mandatory examination results of 5,814 civil servants and considers suspensions, while police arrest three suspected organizers following a joint investigation with the anti-corruption commission. (AFP via The Straits Times)
  • Huachicol fiscal, Organized crime in Mexico
    • Ernesto Ruffo Appel, former governor of Baja California, Mexico, is arrested on charges related to organized crime and fuel smuggling. (Gringo Gazette)
  • Unification Church and politics
    • South Korea's Supreme Court upholds People Power Party lawmaker Kweon Seong-dong's two-year prison sentence for accepting ₩100 million (US$67,400) in illegal political funds from the Unification Church, removing him from the National Assembly. (AFP via The Straits Times)
  • Former Autostrade per l'Italia (ASPI) CEO Giovanni Castellucci is convicted and sentenced to 12 years in prison for his role in the 2018 collapse of the Ponte Morandi in Genoa, Liguria, Italy, which killed 43 people. (ANSA) (TrasportoEuropa)

Politics and elections

  • Dismissal of Mykhailo Fedorov
    • Protests take place in Kyiv and other cities across Ukraine against president Volodymyr Zelenskyy's decision to replace defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov with major-general Yevhenii Khmara. (BBC News) (Reuters)
    • Ukrainian Air Force deputy commander Pavlo Yelizarov resigns from his position in protest of Fedorov's removal as defense minister. (BBC News)

item.title: Current Events - July 26, 2026
item.description:
July 26, 2026 (2026-07-26) (Sunday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Iran war ceasefire
        • Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war, Qatar as a mediator in conflict
          • Iran and the United States submit their responses to a proposal by Pakistan and Qatar to resume talks between the two countries. (The Jerusalem Post)
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy says it has prevented six ships from transiting the Strait of Hormuz. (CNBC)
        • Iranian media reports that an oil tanker exploded in the Strait of Hormuz after it has hit a naval mine. (Middle East Eye)
    • Gaza war
      • Humanitarian aid during the Gaza war
        • Five aid convoys from the United Arab Emirates carrying 938 tonnes of humanitarian aid arrive in Gaza as part of Operation Chivalrous Knight 3. (Gulf Today) (Sharjah24)
      • The Israeli military states that an Hamas unmanned aerial vehicle unit commander was killed in an airstrike yesterday in central Gaza, in violation of the ongoing ceasefire. (The Times of Israel)
    • Yemeni civil war
      • Red Sea crisis
        • Eleven vessels cross the Bab-el-Mandeb strait, according to shipping data from Kpler. (Reuters)
      • Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
        • The Houthis shoot down a Saudi Arabian reconnaissance drone in northwest Yemen. (AFP via The Times of Israel)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) announces that they have recaptured the North Kordofan areas of Umm Qarfa and Juraikh. The SAF also seize control of the National Export Highway (Omdurman–El Obeid), which connects Sudan's capital Khartoum and North Kordofan. (Sudan Horizon) (Sudan Tribune)

Disasters and accidents

  • Vietnamese cargo ship Khoi Nguyen 18 sinks in the South China Sea along the Vietnamese coast. Forty-five people are rescued while 17 more are still missing. (Reuters)

International relations

  • Argentina–Brazil relations
    • Brazil recalls its ambassador to Argentina and summons Argentina's ambassador after Argentine president Javier Milei made remarks deemed derogatory about Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Supreme Court justice Alexandre de Moraes at a political event in São Paulo. (AFP via France 24)
  • Iran–Ukraine relations, Ukraine in the 2026 Iran war
    • The Iranian foreign ministry summons the Ukrainian chargé d'affaires in Tehran over an attack by Ukraine on an Iranian ship in the Caspian Sea that killed an Iranian sailor, calling it a "hostile and criminal act". (CNBC)

Law and crime

  • 2026 Berlin Pride attack
    • A suspect in a recent vehicle-ramming and mass stabbing attack in Berlin, identified as a 21-year-old German citizen of Lebanese descent, is shot and killed by police after allegedly rushing toward officers with a weapon. (CNN)
  • 2026 Seattle Center shooting
    • Three people are killed and four others are injured in a shooting during the annual Bite of Seattle festival in Seattle, Washington, United States. (CNN)

Politics and elections

  • 2027 Salvadoran presidential election
    • El Salvador's Nationalist Republican Alliance nominates former legislator Mayteé Iraheta for president, while the Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front nominates physician Rafael Aguirre. (Reuters)

Science and technology

  • International Space Station expeditions
    • Expedition 74, the joint NASA–Roscosmos–ESA expedition aboard the International Space Station, ends after the Soyuz MS-28 undocks and lands on Earth in Kazakhstan. (CNN)

Sports

  • 2026 Formula One World Championship
    • 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix
      • In auto racing, Formula One announces that Malaysia's Sepang International Circuit will host the rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix in October, under an agreement signed between Bahrain and Malaysia. (Al Jazeera) (Reuters)
  • 2026 All-Ireland Senior Football Championship, Sports-related curses
    • In Gaelic football, the All-Ireland Senior Football Championship concludes with Mayo defeating Kerry in the final to end one of sport's longest-running droughts and a 75-year wait for the title. (ABC News Australia) (ESPN)

  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
        • 2026 Iran war ceasefire
          • United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio says that diplomatic solutions are "still on the table" if Iran ceases attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. (The Jerusalem Post)

          • The Kurdistan Freedom Party reports that eight Iranian Kurdish rebels have been wounded after a drone strike from Iran hit a camp near Erbil, Kurdistan Region, Iraq. (AFP via Arab News)

        • The Israeli military uses the Iron Dome to shoot down fragments from an Iranian missile fired at Aqaba, Jordan, after the Aegis was reportedly used to shoot down the missile. (The Jerusalem Post) (The Times of Israel)

        • The U.S. CENTCOM launches strikes against Iran for a ninth consecutive evening amidst a rise in American casualties. (CNBC) (The Kabul Tribune)
    • Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
      • SDF–Syrian transitional government clashes
        • The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reports that 530 people, including 76 civilians, have been killed in clashes between the post-Assad Syrian Army and the Syrian Democratic Forces over the past months. (Shafaq)

    • 2026 Mali offensives
      • Around 50 Malian soldiers are reported to have been killed in Anéfis, Mali, by the Al-Qaeda-linked Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin and Tuareg Azawad Liberation Front rebels. (The Hindu) (The News Pakistan)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Odesa strikes
      • Ukrainian officials say Russian forces struck a Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship carrying corn off Odesa, killing ten crew members from India and Syria. Eight others are rescued, while the vessel continues burning. (Al Jazeera)

Disasters and accidents

  • 2026 Huancayo earthquake
    • At least six people are killed and 21 others are injured when a Mw 5.5 earthquake strikes the town of Pumpunya in Chongos Bajo District, Chupaca province, Department of Junín, Peru. (Reuters) (notiPerú) (El Comercio Perú)
  • Four people are killed, four others are unaccounted for, and several houses are swept away after a landslide triggered by heavy rainfall hits Mon District, Nagaland, India. (NDTV)
  • Sixty-seven people are rescued and 66 others are reported missing when passenger ferry MV Barima capsizes and sinks near the Pomeroon River in Guyana. (AP)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • Canada bars foreign nationals who have visited the Democratic Republic of the Congo within the previous 21 days, citing the Ebola epidemic. (Reuters)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Delhi Jantar Mantar protests
    • Students hold protests in several cities across India after activist Sonam Wangchuk is arrested and taken to a hospital during his hunger strike calling for education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over the 2026 NEET exam paper leak, with a march on Parliament planned for the following day. (Al Jazeera) (Financial Express)
  • 2026 São Toméan presidential election
    • Santomeans vote to elect the country's president. Incumbent president Carlos Vila Nova seeks a second term in office. (Reuters)

Sports

  • 2026 Esports World Cup
    • League of Legends in esports
      • In esports, Dplus KIA defeats Karmine Corp 3–0 to win the League of Legends title at the 2026 Esports World Cup, extending South Korea's winning streak to three years and securing its first international title since 2020. (DAZN)
  • 2026 FIFA World Cup
    • 2026 FIFA World Cup final
      • In association football, Spain win their second FIFA World Cup title after defeating the defending champions Argentina 1–0 after extra time in the final held at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, United States. Spain's captain Rodri is awarded the Golden Ball. (France 24) (Yahoo! Sports)

      • After winning the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Spain becomes the first country to hold both the men's and women's World Cups, having won the latter in 2023. The men's team extends their international football record of 38 consecutive unbeaten matches, surpassing Italy's record of 37. It also becomes the first team to field two teenagers, Lamine Yamal and Pau Cubarsí, both 19-year-olds, in a FIFA World Cup final. (NPR) (Reuters) (FOX Sports)

item.title: Current Events - July 25, 2026

July 25, 2026 (2026-07-25) (Saturday)

  • history

Armed conflicts and attacks

      • Attacks on refugee camps in the Gaza war, Killing of health workers in the Gaza war
        • A Israeli airstrike reportedly kills a Palestinian medic at the Nuseirat refugee camp in the central Gaza Strip. (Reuters via The Times of Israel)
      • An Israeli airstrike reportedly kills senior brigadier general Abdel-Nasser Al-Maqadma, the head of the Hamas police force in the North Gaza Governorate, Gaza. (Asharq Al-Awsat) (Reuters)
      • The Israeli military confirms that they have killed several Hamas militants over the past few weeks, including a Nukhba forces cell commander who took part in the Kissufim massacre during the October 7, 2023 attacks. (The Times of Israel)
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • The naval forces of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claims to have stopped four vessels from transiting the Strait of Hormuz. (Middle East Eye)
      • July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
        • Iranian health ministry spokesperson Hossein Kermanpour reports no U.S. military strikes against Iran, after 13 consecutive nights of strikes by the U.S. Central Command against the country. (NBC News)
        • The United States halts strikes against Iran after government officials reportedly saw a potential opening to resume diplomatic efforts and talks. (Al-Monitor) (AP)
    • Red Sea crisis, Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
      • Two people are injured by Saudi-led coalition airstrikes on Hodeidah, Houthi-controlled Yemen. A Patriot battery operated by the Greek military intercepts two ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis at Aramco facilities in Yanbu and Jizan, Saudi Arabia. (CNBC) (NBC News) (Al Jazeera)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Ukrainian officials say a Russian drone strike on a postal facility in Sumy has killed two people. (AFP via BGNES)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • Kordofan campaign
      • Darfur Joint Protection Force spokesperson Mutawakkil Ali Wakil confirms that, in coordination with the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), that the joint force have retaken control of Umm Sayala, North Kordofan, Sudan, with 38 members of the Rapid Support Forces confirmed to have been killed. (Sudan Horizon)
      • The SAF and Darfur Joint Protection Force recapture Jebrat al Sheikh alongside the North Kordofan towns of Bara and Al-Baraka. Additionally, Darfur governor Minni Arko Minawi confirms the recaptures. (Sudan Tribune)

Disasters and accidents

  • Snyder Fire
    • A fourth firefighter dies from injuries sustained in a wildfire at the Colorado–Utah border in the United States on June 27. (The Guardian) (KUSA)
  • The death toll from the flash floods in Assam, India, rises to 62, after fourteen more fatalities are confirmed. (NDTV)
  • At least 35 people are killed and 30 others are injured when two buses collide on the Deir ez-Zor–Damascus road in Syria. (Reuters)
  • Two people are killed when a Tecnam P2010 aircraft crashes into a home in Ganderkesee, Lower Saxony, Germany. (DPA via South China Morning Post)
  • One person is killed and at least 22 others are injured in a five-alarm fire in Flushing, New York City, United States. (WNBC)

International relations

  • Brazil–United States relations
    • Brazil denies visas to two U.S. state department officials seeking election-related meetings in Brasília, citing risks of "political exploitation". The U.S. state department says the visit concerns electoral integrity and freedom of expression. (AFP via Arab News)

Law and crime

  • 2026 Berlin Pride attack
    • Abdul Ballout, a 21-year-old Lebanese-German, drives into a crowd at the pride festival in Berlin, Germany, killing a person and injuring 29 others. A suspect is on the run. (CNN)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Brazilian general election
    • Brazil's Liberal Party formally nominates Rio de Janeiro senator Flávio Bolsonaro, former president Jair Bolsonaro's son, as its presidential candidate in the upcoming election. (AFP via Philippine Daily Inquirer) (Reuters)
  • 2026 Delhi Jantar Mantar protests
    • Indian education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns after protests over alleged entrance-examination leaks and broader education-system irregularities. His resignation marks the Modi government's first major concession to the demonstrations. (AFP via Le Monde)

item.title: Current Events - July 18, 2026
item.description:
July 18, 2026 (2026-07-18) (Saturday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • 2026 Iran war
    • 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
      • 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
        • The Bahraini military intercepts projectiles fired from Iran. (DPA via Yahoo News)
      • 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
        • The U.S. Central ​Command (CENTCOM) reports that two American troops have been "killed in action" in Jordan, bringing the total casualties for American troops to 16. (Reuters) (The Wall Street Journal)
      • 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
        • Kuwait says Iranian attacks have struck a second power and desalination plant in two days, causing a fire and shutting several generating units, while other attacks injure firefighters and a worker and temporarily disrupt flights from Kuwait International Airport. (AFP via Vanguard)
        • An oil facility is damaged, according to the Kuwait Petroleum Corporation. (PBS)
      • 2026 Iranian strikes on Saudi Arabia
        • Axios reports that Iran has launched a ballistic missile at a United States base in Saudi Arabia, making it the first direct attack by Iran on the country since targeting a petrochemical complex in Jubail. (Financial Times)
    • 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
      • Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi says that the United States has violated the terms of the Islamabad Memorandum and that Iran is "no longer implementing them". (PBS)
    • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
      • The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, in a statement published by IRNA, report that two oil tankers have exploded after hitting mines south in the Strait of Hormuz. However, the U.S. Central Command disputes the claims on X as "false". (AFP via Arab News)
      • The Philippine foreign affairs department reports that four Philippine-registered vessels carrying 81 seafarers have safely transited through the Strait of Hormuz. The vessels are identified as the MV Lyng Trader, MV Western Doncaster, MV Vivian Trader, and MV Eva Fuji. (GMA Network)
    • July 2026 United States strikes against Iran
      • In the seventh day of renewed U.S. strikes, civilian infrastructure, including a desalination plant in Jask, are damaged, cutting off the access to water for 10,000 civilians. (IRNA) (BBC Persian (in Persian))
      • Communications services in Iran's Hormozgan province are disrupted after U.S. strikes damaged 116 radio towers there. (BBC News) (BBC Persian (in Persian))
      • The U.S. CENTCOM launches a new wave of strikes for an eighth consecutive night against IRGC targets in response to two American service members killed in Jordan. (The Hill)
  • Mali War
    • 2026 Mali offensives
      • The Al-Qaeda-linked Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin and Tuareg Azawad Liberation Front rebels ambush a Malian military convoy in the Gao Region of Mali. (Al Jazeera) (AP)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war, Aerial warfare in the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Moscow Oblast governor Andrey Vorobyov and Tambov Oblast head Yevgeny Pervyshov say Ukrainian drone attacks killed seven workers and injure 49 others at Wildberries warehouses in Kotovsk and Elektrostal, Russia, while another strike ignites an oil facility. Ukraine says the warehouses support Russian drone production. (Reuters)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • Arab League secretary general Nabil Fahmy and U.S. envoy Massad Boulos reach an agreement to establish a regular framework for joint coordination for a ceasefire in the ongoing civil war in Sudan. (Sudan Tribune)
  • Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
    • An insurgent is killed and five others are injured during a counterterrorism operation that foiled a terrorist plot in Wana, South Waziristan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. (Dawn)

Business and economy

  • Belgium–Israel relations, International reactions to the Gaza war
    • Belgium approves an import ban on goods from Israeli settlements. (Al Jazeera)
  • Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
    • Kuwait Airways reschedules most of its flights due to the country's airspace being closed amidst ongoing Iranian attacks. (Middle East Eye)
    • Iran's Hormozgan province water and wastewater company announces that United States airstrikes have damaged desalination equipment, cutting off water to about 10,000 people. (Middle East Eye)

Disasters and accidents

  • Krokstadelva fire
    • Over 100 houses burn down in the Norwegian town Krokstadelva. (NOS)
  • Nine people are killed and nine others are injured after an unauthorized firecracker factory explodes in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India. (NDTV) (Xinhua)
  • Five people are killed and two others are injured in a workplace accident in Thanh Hóa province, Vietnam. (Xinhua)
  • Five people, including three women, drown in the Godavari River whilst fishing near Polavaram district, India. (The Hindu)
  • Four people are killed, four more are missing, and seven others are injured after torrential rains and flash floods hit a mountainous village in Lai Châu province, Vietnam. (AA)

Law and crime

  • Turkey–Islamic State conflict
    • Turkey’s interior ministry announces the arrest of 119 people linked to ISIS. (AFP via Al Arabiya)

Politics and elections

  • Magyar Government
    • Hungarian president Tamás Sulyok signs the 17th amendment to the nation's constitution, which will end his term in office at midnight the following day. (BBC News)
  • Jens Spahn resigns as leader of the governing CDU/CSU alliance in Germany's Bundestag amid criticism after he and his husband became parents through surrogacy, despite Germany's ban and his party's opposition to the practice. (AFP via Channels TV)

Science and technology

  • Space industry of India
    • Skyroot Aerospace successfully launches Vikram-1, India's first privately built orbital rocket, from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Andhra Pradesh, carrying small satellite payloads into low Earth orbit on its maiden flight. (AFP via Asharq Al-Awsat)

Sports

  • 2026 FIFA World Cup
    • In association football, England beats France 6–4 in the highest-scoring third-place playoff in FIFA World Cup history, securing their best result since winning the tournament in 1966. (BBC Sport)
    • French footballer Kylian Mbappé scores twice to become the highest-scoring player in World Cup history, and the first player to score 10 goals in a single World Cup since Germany's Gerd Müller in 1970. (BBC Sport)
  • 2026 Diamond League
    • At the London Athletics Meet, British runner Josh Kerr sets a new world record of 3:42.66 for the mile. The previous record of 3:43.13 by Hicham El Guerrouj had been set in 1999. (BBC Sport)

item.title: Current Events - July 27, 2026
item.description:
July 27, 2026 (2026-07-27) (Monday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations
        • Iran and the United States pause strikes as the U.S. allows additional time for negotiations and Iran suspends retaliatory attacks against U.S. allies. (AFP via The Manila Times)
      • Saudi Arabia in the 2026 Iran war
        • Saudi Arabia's defense ministry reports intercepting drones fired by Iran-backed Iraqi militias from inside Iraq, which targeted oil facilities in eastern Saudi Arabia and the Riyadh area. (France 24)

      • Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict, Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
        • The Houthis launch a drone attack that damages the Abqaiq oil field in eastern Saudi Arabia. (BBC Persian) (France 24)

    • Kordofan campaign
      • Siege of El Obeid
        • Drone strikes are reported in El-Obeid, North Kordofan, Sudan, hours after the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) secured the National Export Highway, which connects Sudan's capital Khartoum and North Kordofan. (AFP via France 24) (The Defense Post)
      • The Sudanese Doctors Network reports that the main hospital in Jebrat al Sheikh District, North Kordofan, has been looted and turned into a military barrack. (Sudan Tribune)
      • SAF general and leader Abdel Fattah al-Burhan visits the newly captured areas in North Kordofan alongside Sudan Shield Forces leader Abu Aqla Kaikal and Darfur Governor Minni Arko Minnawi. (Sudan Tribune)

Business and economy

  • Canada–United States relations
    • 2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico
      • The Gordie Howe International Bridge, which connects between Detroit, Michigan, U.S., and Windsor, Ontario, Canada, officially opens to traffic after months of delay due to the countries' trade war and the U.S. imposition of tariffs on Canada. (Detroit Free Press) (Global News)
  • Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
    • Singapore's monetary authority tightens monetary policy for the second time in three months by increasing the Singapore dollar's appreciation rate against a trade-weighted currency basket, citing rising import costs and inflation risks caused by the Iran war. (AFP via South China Morning Post)

Disasters and accidents

  • Wildfires in 2026
    • 2026 France wildfires
      • Wildfires continue in the Gironde region near Bordeaux, France, as president Emmanuel Macron describes it as "the worst fire-related crisis since World War II." (AP)
  • 2026 Pacific hurricane season
    • Hurricane Genevieve strengthens into a category 5 pacific hurricane, the first in the Pacific region since 2024. (The Independent)
  • The death toll from heavy rains and flooding in Pakistan since June increases to 107 people killed and at least 344 others injured. (Al Jazeera)
  • A landslide occurs at the Gold Ridge Mine in Guadalcanal, Solomon Islands. Local media reports 10 bodies recovered, while the National Referral Hospital says it expects fatalities. (AFP via BSS)

Health and environment

  • Sudanese cholera epidemic
    • The General Coordination for Refugees and Displaced Persons in Darfur reports seven cholera cases across the Darfur region in displacement camps between July 5 and July 25. (Sudan Tribune)
  • The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approves a new blood test for colorectal cancer screenings in older adults, including those above age 45. (Reuters) (MedPage Today)

International relations

  • Kuwait–Pakistan relations
    • Kuwait approved the Kuwait–Pakistan Defence Cooperation Agreement, a five-year framework for defence cooperation between the two countries covering military training, exchanges, defence technology, logistics and cooperation between their armed forces.(Anadolu Ajansı)(Jordan News)
  • Brazil–Lithuania relations
    • The Lithuanian government registers a resolution to open an embassy in Brasilia, Brazil, in October. The country currently has a consulate-general in São Paulo. (LRT)
  • Romania–Russia relations, Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Romania recalls its ambassador to Russia, declares a Russian embassy employee persona non grata, and summons Russia's ambassador after three Russian drones violated Romanian airspace between July 24 and 26. (Xinhua)
  • Chad states its intention to withdraw from the International Criminal Court, citing limited effectiveness and disproportionate attention to African cases. (AFP via Courthouse News Service)

Law and crime

  • The Seoul Central District Court gives former South Korean president Yoon Suk Yeol an 18-month suspended sentence for false statements made during his 2022 election campaign. If upheld, the ruling may void his victory and require Yoon's People Power Party to repay campaign funds. (AFP via The Japan Times)
  • Five people are killed and another is injured in a home invasion and shooting in Gugulethu, Cape Town, South Africa. (News24)
  • Three women are wounded in a mass stabbing near the Porte de Clichy station in Paris, France. The perpetrator is detained. (Reuters) (The Telegraph)

Politics and elections

  • Politics of Nicaragua
    • Nicaraguan co-president Rosario Murillo announces that a legislative vote on a proposed constitutional reform that would exclude opposition parties from future elections has been postponed until September. (AFP via GMA News Online)

            • Mediators Pakistan and Qatar propose a 10-day ceasefire in an effort to revive the Islamabad Memorandum signed last month. (MENA via The New Arab) (Reuters)

        • 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan

        • The United States imposes new sanctions upon the Sudanese military junta, alleging the use of chemical weapons including chlorine gas in the civil war. (RFI)

      • The Iraqi military say that they have destroyed six ISIS hideouts in Kirkuk, Iraq. (Iraqi News)

      • U.S. president Donald Trump signs another executive order imposing 50% tariffs on many Canadian goods, including USMCA-covered products, citing alleged discriminatory trade practices. The duties take effect in 30 days, with exemptions for energy, potash, and products under sector-specific tariffs. (AFP via Vanguard) (CBC News)

    • 2026 Iran war fuel crisis
      • The nationwide gas prices in the United States exceeds US$4 per gallon, the highest since June 17. (AP) (NBC News)

    • Sir Keir Starmer resigns as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, and is succeeded by Andy Burnham. (CNN) (The Guardian) (The Telegraph)

    • Nicaraguan co-president Daniel Ortega announces that the country will hold no further elections in order to "build a wall" against the political opposition. (The Guardian)

      • July 2026 West Bank unrest
        • Clashes in Tell, Nablus, kill four Palestinians and two Israelis after a confrontation between settlers and locals in the town. Subsequent settler attacks in the West Bank injure at least 10 Palestinians. (Haaretz) (The New York Times)
    • Red Sea crisis, Saudi-led intervention in the Yemeni civil war
      • The Houthis deny reports that they have closed the Bab-el-Mandeb and state that they are not seeking to close it, reaffirming that they have only established a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia. (DW) (Middle East Eye)
      • Saudi Arabia strikes Houthi military sites in Hodeidah, Yemen, after a long hiatus in response to the movement's attacks on maritime shipping, while the militant group vows to retaliate. (Reuters)
  • Russo-Ukrainian war
    • Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • Ukrainian strikes on Wildberries warehouses
        • A Wildberries logistic hub in Russia-occupied Crimea is hit by Ukrainian drones and catches fire. (RBC-Ukraine)
        • Ukrainian drones also hit Wildberries logistics hubs in Saint Petersburg and Tver, Russia. (Kyiv Independent)
    • Kyiv strikes
      • Ukrainian officials say a Russian ballistic missile strike on a private training ground hosting a defence-industry event in the Kyiv Oblast killed 10 people and injured nearly 100. Prosecutors investigate possible negligence in organizing the event. (Reuters)
    • Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war
      • A Romanian F-16 ​fighter jet shot down a Russian Geran-2 drone near Padina, Buzău County, that had entered its airspace for the first ‌time. (Euronews)
  • Sudanese civil war
    • Kordofan campaign
      • The North Kordofan government reports that 15 civilians in the Burbur area south of El-Obeid, Sudan have been killed by a Rapid Support Forces drone strike. (Sudan Tribune)
  • Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
    • At least 27 people are killed, including 12 militants, in an attack on a security check post in Tank District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. (Hindustan Times)

Business and economy

  • Tariffs in the second Trump administration
    • 2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico
      • The Gordie Howe International Bridge, which connects between Detroit, Michigan, U.S., and Windsor, Ontario, Canada, ceremonially opens, with Canadian officials marking the opening ceremony of the bridge with the absence of American officials amidst ongoing trade tensions. (Detroit Free Press) (Reuters)
  • Proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance
    • Paramount announces that they have agreed to delay its US$111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery amidst lawsuits from twelve U.S. state attorneys general. (AFP via France 24) (The Hill)

Disasters and accidents

  • Wildfires in 2026
    • 2026 France wildfires
      • French authorities evacuate more than 110,000 people from Cap Ferret, Gironde, by land and sea as an uncontrolled wildfire burns over 19,000 hectares, destroys 80 homes, and threatens the peninsula’s only access road. (The Guardian)
    • 2026 Spain wildfires
      • Spanish interior minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska declares a national emergency over wildfires in the Community of Madrid and the Province of Ávila, placing the Military Emergencies Unit in command. Authorities evacuate more than 10,000 people as three major fires remain uncontrolled. (AA)
  • Thirteen people are killed and two others are injured after a heavy boulder rolled down a hill and hit moving vehicles in Chamba District, India. (Xinhua)
  • Five people are killed and three others are injured when a soil collapse buries a house in Hongtong County, Shanxi, China. (Reuters)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Ebola epidemic
    • Oxford University reports the first volunteer that has been injected with the Ebola vaccine aimed at targeting the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain of Ebola that is causing a outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. (AFP via GMA News Online)
  • 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
    • The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reports that the ongoing cyclosporiasis outbreak, which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis, has spread to an additional four states: Illinois, Kansas, Oklahoma, and Pennsylvania. (CNBC)
    • The U.S. state of Michigan surpasses 8,100 cases of cyclosporiasis. (CBS News)
  • Dengue fever outbreaks
    • The Sudan Doctors Union reports a dengue fever outbreak in Sudan's Blue Nile state, killing 39 people and leaving 300 infected. (Sudan Tribune)
  • Measles resurgence in the United States
    • The U.S. CDC reports 2,318 confirmed measles cases in the country during the first seven months of 2026, marking the highest annual total since 1991. (AFP via Euractiv)

International relations

  • International sanctions against Iran
    • Iran–European Union relations
      • The European Union sanctions five Iranian judges over alleged human rights violations and Ashiyane cyber group founder Nima Salehi, whom it accuses of cooperating with Iranian authorities to suppress information. (Reuters)
    • United States sanctions against Iran
      • The U.S. treasury department announces sanctions against nine firms and four people associated with sanctioned Iranian financer Babak Zanjani after attempting to evade previous sanctions. (Reuters)
  • International Criminal Court investigation in Venezuela
    • Venezuelan foreign minister Félix Plasencia says the country will withdraw from the International Criminal Court (ICC), citing alleged geographic bias. The ICC says it has not received formal notice and that existing investigations and cooperation obligations remain unaffected. (AFP via RFI)
  • Mexico–United States relations, Mexican war on drugs
    • The U.S. state department, in coordination with the Mexican finance ministry, sanctions over 50 Mexican individuals and companies allegedly linked to the Jalisco New Generation Cartel. (Bloomberg) (El País)

Law and crime

  • 2020 Phala Phala robbery
    • A South African court temporarily halts the parliament's impeachment inquiry into president Cyril Ramaphosa over the theft of US$580,000 from his farm, pending his challenge to a report finding possible constitutional violations. (Reuters)
  • Eight people are killed, including six children, in an arson and shooting attack at a house in Grand Haven Charter Township, Michigan, United States. (ABC News) (The Indian Express)
  • Diplomatic sources say International Criminal Court member states voted to remove chief prosecutor Karim Ahmad Khan following sexual misconduct allegations. (Al Jazeera) (CNN)
  • Prosecutors say thieves stole a 2,500-year-old gold Celtic necklace from the Musée du Pays Châtillonnais in Châtillon-sur-Seine, Côte-d'Or, France, after breaking its display case during opening hours. The artifact belongs to the Vix treasure. (AFP via The Manila Times)

Politics and elections

  • Protests against the dismissal of Mykhailo Fedorov
    • For the ninth consecutive day, thousands continue to protest in Kyiv, Ukraine, demanding Mykhailo Fedorov's reinstatement as Minister of Defence. (The Kyiv Independent)
  • Bangladeshi president Mohammed Shahabuddin resigns from office, citing health reasons. (Reuters)
  • Forty deputies of the Polish Sejm leave the Law and Justice party as part of a dispute between party leader Jarosław Kaczyński and member Mateusz Morawiecki. (AP) (Polsat in Polish)
  • The White House Correspondents' Dinner is held at the Waldorf Astoria hotel in Washington, D.C., after being rescheduled following the assassination attempt at the Washington Hilton in April 2026. This is the first White House Correspondents' Dinner attended by U.S. President Donald Trump, after he previously skipped every dinner during his first term. (Politico) (NPR)

Science and technology

  • The SpaceX Starship test flight 13, the first to successfully deploy operational Starlink satellites, successfully lands in the Indian Ocean intact. (CNN)

item.title: Current Events - July 17, 2026
item.description:
July 17, 2026 (2026-07-17) (Friday)
  • edit
  • history
  • watch

Armed conflicts and attacks

  • Middle Eastern crisis
    • 2026 Iran war
      • 2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries
        • 2026 Iranian strikes on Bahrain
          • Iran says that it has launched ballistic missile and drone strikes at targets in Bahrain, including a drone vessel depot, an artificial intelligence center used for targeting, and the Al-Sakhir Air Base, as part of the 11th phase of its Saegheh operation. (AA) (Middle East Monitor)
        • 2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan
          • Jordan reports having intercepted projectiles fired from Iran. (AA)
        • 2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait
          • Iranian strikes damage a desalination plant and a power plant in Kuwait, according to the Kuwaiti energy ministry. (AP) (CNBC)
        • 2026 Iranian strikes on Oman
          • The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy launches attacks on radar facilities in Oman. (AA)
        • 2026 Iranian strikes on Syria
          • Iranian state media reports that Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps have targeted a United States Special Operations Command in Al-Tanf in response to the killing of Iranian soldiers in Iranshahr, Sistan and Baluchestan province. (Arab News)
        • 2026 Iranian strikes on Qatar
          • The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Aerospace Force launches an attack at Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar, and claims to have caused damage to equipment there, while Qatar's armed forces claim to have intercepted Iranian attacks. (AA)
      • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis
        • The U.S. military's Central Command (CENTCOM) confirms that they have destroyed the Chah Bahar Shahid Kalantari Port surveillance tower in Chabahar Port yesterday, which was allegedly used by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps for tracking commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz. (The Times of Israel)
      • 2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region
        • Iranian drone strikes near Erbil, Kurdistan Region, Iraq, kill eight Kurdish rebels and injure several more. (AFP via The Times of Israel)
      • CENTCOM launches strikes against Iran for a seventh consecutive night. (The Guardian)
    • Gaza war
      • Around eight Palestinians are reported to be killed in an airstrike on a funeral in central Gaza. (AA)
      • The Israeli military and Shin Bet confirm that they have killed Hamas commander Anas Mahmoud Ahmad Hamdan, who served as a "right-hand man" of former Al-Qassam Brigades commander Mohammed Deif, in an airstrike in Khan Yunis, Gaza Strip. (The Times of Israel)

Business and economy

  • Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war
    • 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis, Iraq–Syria relations
      • Iraq and Syria sign a memorandum of understanding to rehabilitate the Kirkuk–Baniyas pipeline to bypass to the Strait of Hormuz. (Middle East Eye)

Disasters and accidents

  • Wildfires in 2026
    • 2026 United States wildfires
      • 2026 Minnesota wildfires
        • The United States Forest Service reports that wildfires in northern Minnesota has reached over 77,000 acres, prompting evacuations in the area. (KARE TV) (KAAL)
    • 2026 Canadian wildfires
      • Over 900 wildfires are reported across Canada, including 43 new active blazes, prompting evacuations across the country. (CTV News) (BNN Bloomberg)
      • The U.S. state of Connecticut's Department of Energy and Environmental Protection deploys firefighters to assist with wildfire efforts in Quebec, Canada. (CT.Gov) (WVIT)
  • 2026 Venezuela earthquakes
    • The confirmed death toll from the doublet earthquakes that struck northern Venezuela rose to 5,069. (AP)
  • 2026 Chiapas earthquake
    • A strong Mw 7.3 earthquake strikes near the coast of Chiapas, Mexico. Tsunami warnings were issued and damage is unknown. (BBC News) (The Weather Network)
  • Eight people are killed, ten others are rescued and 34 are reported missing when a landslide buries multiple houses and residential buildings in Pengshui, Chongqing, China. (ABC News) (India Today)
  • Four people are killed and nine others are injured after a head-on collision between two overspeeding cars along the N-25 National Highway, Wadh, Balochistan, Pakistan (Dawn)
  • A nine-vehicle pile-up in Deli Serdang, North Sumatra, Indonesia kills at least four and injures eight others. (Xinhua)
  • Chilean authorities report that a storm system that began affecting the country on Thursday has killed three people, injured seven others, damaged more than 800 homes, displaced hundreds and left around 400,000 people without electricity across 10 regions. (Xinhua) (Reuters)
  • A nine-story building under construction near Conakry, Guinea, collapses due to heavy rainfall, killing three people and injuring several others. (Xinhua)
  • Two citizens are killed from weather-related incidents and 53,000 homes are reported to be without power during severe thunderstorms across several regions of France. (AA)
  • A large fire breaks out among terraced houses in Krokstadelva, Drammen, Norway, spreading rapidly between multiple housing blocks and prompting mass evacuations; the municipality declares a crisis and calls in fire crews from eight neighboring municipalities. (Reuters) (VG)

Health and environment

  • 2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak
    • The death tolls from the measles outbreak in Bangladesh reaches 780 after one child is reported to have died from the disease by the Directorate General of Health Services. (Dhaka Tribune)
  • 2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak
    • Taylor Farms recalls their iceburg lettuce, traced through a farm in Mexico, amidst the ongoing cyclosporiasis outbreak in the United States, which is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis. (Forbes)
    • Michigan, U.S., surpasses 5,000 cases of cyclosporiasis. (The Detroit News)

Law and crime

  • A civilian dies and a police officer and the suspected gunman are wounded in a shooting in Nørresundby, North Jutland, Denmark, after officers responding to a reported fire are met with gunfire. (AP) (TV2)
  • The Ontario Court of Appeal finds Canadian far-right activist and Freedom Convoy organizer Pat King "guilty of intimidation" and orders a re-sentencing. (CBC) (Toronto Star)
  • Japan enacts a law criminalizing public damage, removal or defacement of the national flag, punishable by up to two years in prison or a ¥200,000 (US$1,200) fine. (AFP via France 24)
  • Turkish authorities detain 67 irregular migrants and five other suspected smugglers following a sailboat interception off the coast of Muğla, Türkiye. (Xinhua)

International relations

  • Hong Kong–United States relations
    • The United States allows its national emergency over Hong Kong's national security law to expire while retaining the underlying executive order and most related sanctions. (AFP via New Straits Times)

Politics and elections

  • 2026 Labour Party leadership election
    • Andy Burnham is elected as the new leader of the British Labour Party. He will formally succeed Keir Starmer as prime minister on Monday. (BBC News) (CNN) (The Guardian)
  • Dismissal of Mykhailo Fedorov
    • Protests continue for a second day in Kyiv near the Office of the President of Ukraine, demanding the return of Mykhailo Fedorov as Minister of Defence and the resignation of Oleksandr Syrskyi as the Commander-in-Chief. (Reuters)
  • Japanese imperial succession debate
    • Japan's National Diet amends the Imperial Household Law to allow unmarried male descendants of former imperial branches to rejoin the family and permit royal women to retain status after marrying commoners, while preserving male-only succession. (AFP via ABS-CBN News)
